title: Mega Dormitory completion plan
purpose: A sequential plan for finishing the accepted game, not another unbounded list of possible improvements.

baseline.verification: Previously verified: 42 suites, headless memory checks, hardware/software rendered workflows and older saves. This planning update does not rerun or upgrade that evidence.
retain: Ownership, economy, physical jobs, queues, construction, transport and core NPC routines
Households/storage, companies/equity, estates, investigations and medical/death systems
Bounded connected-floor fire/smoke/cargo loss, multilingual UI, saved controls and procedural sound

platform_target: Complete Linux and Windows player packages; support claims require actual platform validation.
cancelled_scope: Floating island / explorable outside city / separate outside hospital
Creative mode (superseded by Survival, Manager and Cheat)

current.next_action: Connect face-to-face and device communication to information about services, work, trade, help, threats and witnessed events.

execution_policy: Read this tracker and completion-plan.md on every implementation continuation; resume the current task rather than choosing a new theme.
Execute milestone IDs in order. Finish and verify the current milestone before starting the next; do not restart already delivered baseline systems.
Work on one milestone at a time. A prerequisite bug fix belongs to that milestone; record what it unblocks and return immediately to the current task.
Acknowledge a user priority/scope change with a dated change_log entry; do not silently reorder, add release blockers or replace the accepted design.
New optional ideas go to future_ideas, not the release backlog. A required connecting task goes under its existing owner milestone with a reason.
Keep each accepted feature coherent across rules, actual movement/actions, NPC choice, player interaction, ownership/economy, interruption/death, saves, localization and presentation.
Complete a task only with relevant evidence; complete a milestone only when all its tasks and acceptance criteria pass. Test counts alone never prove feature or game completion.

Use appropriate focused/regression checks and real rendered play; broaden/repeat only after relevant changes, failures or unresolved concerns. Do not rerun the entire native suite for plan-only edits.
Preserve player saves and the old browser prototype. Verify/install/publish working code checkpoints using the already authorized project workflow.

Before ending an implementation turn, update task status, evidence, blocker/next action and next task pointer; report completed IDs and the exact next ID. Do not ask what to do next when this plan already answers it.
Only M32 passing its complete release gate permits an overall finished/shippable claim. An individual code checkpoint or portable archive remains a development update until then.
definition_of_done: Rules and required edge/failure cases behave as specified; no decorative-only substitute for a required action.
Player and NPC actors use real movement, staffing, tools, resources, ownership, payments and permissions.
Interruption, cancellation, competing claims, surrender, death, emigration and changed availability retain valid state.
Persistent state round-trips and required older/browser fixtures continue without lost or duplicated resources.
English, French and Chinese names/text/input remain coherent; required UI and animation/feedback are usable.
Relevant invariant, regression, CPU/GPU and memory checks pass; appropriate rendered and manual play evidence is recorded.
Limits and remaining work are attributed to another numbered milestone or an explicit future idea, never silently declared complete.

tasks.title: Classify every accepted feature as implemented, partial, missing or explicitly cancelled; archive-only imports count as partial.

tasks.title: Write reproducible end-to-end acceptance scenarios and a severity-ranked regression list; record baseline hardware and package behaviour.
evidence: docs/acceptance-scenarios.md: 38 procedures/pass conditions mapped to owner milestones.
docs/baseline-evidence.json and docs/evidence/m00-daily-life.log: hardware, focused checks, isolated generation/simulation and rendered daily-life baseline.

evidence: docs/feature-inventory.md: frozen finite scope and bounded-model decisions.

acceptance: Every accepted requirement and discovered retained browser feature has an owner milestone and a concrete acceptance scenario.
The existing 714b444 baseline is retained; no completed subsystem is restarted merely because a new session begins.
Any proposed extra feature is labelled future work unless required by an accepted scenario; scope changes have a dated explanation.
acceptance_evidence: 38/38 requirement IDs and 14/14 parity rows have valid owners and concrete AC01–AC38 scenarios in acceptance-register.json.
Code baseline 714b444 remains intact; native saves and all three browser copies were untouched during the isolated checks.
Finite scope rules explicitly exclude the cancelled city/Creative mode and distinguish bounded gameplay from additional unaccepted simulators; only existing milestone tasks own the gaps.

tests/social_tests.cpp: eighteen passing focused rule/migration/privacy/regression checks.

tasks.title: Connect face-to-face and device communication to information about services, work, trade, help, threats and witnessed events.
Use personality, history and relationships when choosing help, refusal, cooperation, theft, reporting and surrender.
Expose readable relationship/history controls and verify that information travels through real actors or available devices.

acceptance: A repeated interaction changes later decisions; an unobserved event does not magically become shared knowledge.
Two residents with different personalities/history make different explainable choices in the same resource conflict.
Player and NPC relationship/information state survives interruptions, death and reload without identity changes.

milestones.title: Complete household provisioning and independent planning

Finish independent buying, selling, career changes, saving and small-business investment using actual affordability and travel.
Handle unavailable stock/staff, queues, interrupted delivery, job loss, illness and changing household membership with coherent replanning.

acceptance: An unattended household can buy, receive, store, collect and consume supplies through normal physical and financial rules.
Reserved money/goods cannot be spent or shared twice, and urgent needs can interrupt a longer plan safely.
The player can inspect why a plan is waiting or was changed; recurring benign availability changes do not create failure spam.

acceptance: A dependent receives actual care/resources from available actors; missing care has visible, causal consequences.
Birth, ageing and death continue through saves and migrated browser fixtures with consistent identities and names.
Family features satisfy the retained prototype scenarios instead of merely retaining their data in an archive.

milestones.title: Complete displacement, compensation and forced eviction

milestones.title: Structural damage, failure and repair

acceptance: A failing structural element removes the same support in physics, paths and rendering; occupants fall or evacuate causally.

Repair restores only paid, supplied and attended work; ownership, claims, debris and deaths are not erased.

acceptance: People, furniture and vehicles cannot be used to pass through walls, floors or one another by ordinary controls.

acceptance: Audible events correspond to actual nearby actions and stop/reset correctly; important hazards remain understandable when muted.

Interaction feedback makes success, waiting, rejection and completion clear without drowning out the world.

milestones.title: Finish browser parity, persistence and platform readiness

tasks.title: Close every non-cancelled parity gap from M00 and validate native continuation of imported family, items, history and rules.
Finalize versioned native migrations, named-slot previews, backups, recovery, interruption and installation-independent saves.
Finish Linux/Windows builds, platform input/audio/filesystem support and relocatable player packages.
Run the old/new world-size, mode, language and corruption compatibility matrix and record unsupported cases explicitly.

acceptance: No accepted browser feature is marked complete solely because its data is archived; all parity scenarios are implemented or explicitly superseded by the user.
Older supported saves migrate without duplicating payments/items or discarding identities/contracts; damaged slots have a usable recovery path.
Linux and Windows candidates build and launch with their packaged resources; a platform is not labelled supported without its actual verification.

milestones.title: GPU parallel simulation and streamed world scaling

tasks.title: Profile the completed game on the recorded reference GPU and CPU fallback before choosing expensive work to offload.
Implement streamed/cached geometry/textures, crowd/detail LOD and GPU animation sampling where it improves actual play.
Offload suitable resident/crowd/needs or other large parallel work with explicit CPU reference checks and safe synchronization.
Meet the documented default-world frame, responsiveness, memory and simulation-progress budgets without deleting features.

acceptance: The 100,000-resident/2,000-floor world keeps up at 1× compressed time with bounded processing backlog and responsive controls.
Reference GPU target: 1080p/60 FPS target, p95 frame time at most 33 ms and p99 at most 50 ms in the recorded dense-play route; ordinary UI responses at most 100 ms.
The recorded CPU-only 720p preset targets at least 15 FPS and usable controls; CPU/GPU paths preserve the same validated rules, ownership and accounting.

milestones.title: Long-run scarcity balance and adversarial simulation

tasks.title: Run at least five recorded default-size seeds for thirty game days, plus small/large/extreme configuration and disaster scenarios.
Tune initial shortages, queues, rents, wages, subscriptions, construction costs, migration, happiness and investment against actual outcomes.
Track crashes, conservation, resource duplication, unsupported residents, task failures, starvation loops, deadlocks and company/death cleanup.
Fix systemic failures and preserve failing seeds/replays as meaningful regression cases rather than masking errors.

acceptance: Default scarcity produces meaningful long queues and hard choices while sustained survival has a demonstrated viable route.
Any depopulation, insolvency or game over has a traceable gameplay cause, not an impossible schedule or broken service loop.
Across the recorded matrix, accounts/resources remain consistent and eligible unobstructed tasks do not recur as permanent failure loops.

milestones.title: Complete player acceptance and localization/accessibility QA

tasks.title: Play a fresh Survival run from move-in through needs, queues, real work, shopping/delivery, better housing and a business/vehicle purchase.
Play Manager through staffing, construction, displacement, service investment, emergencies and succession; test full Cheat controls and possession.
Exercise robbery/conflict, surrender/arrest/cells, rescue/treatment, disaster recovery, inheritance and each game-over/reload route.
Repeat required flows across English/French/Chinese, input/scaling/focus configurations and supported hardware, recording actual manual play as well as automated replays.

acceptance: Every accepted requirement has a completed player-visible acceptance scenario and evidence in the coverage register.
There are no hidden developer-only controls, placeholder options or language-dependent identity/payment bugs in the required flows.
Critical controls and dangers remain discoverable/readable with accessible alternatives; automated passing tests alone cannot close this milestone.

milestones.title: Release candidate, clean-install verification and version 1.0

tasks.title: Build reproducible supported-platform candidates with integrity manifests, licences, version information, controls/help and troubleshooting.
Test clean installation and relocation on machines/environments without the development tree or compiler; verify save separation and upgrade/recovery.
Close all required milestones and P0/P1 defects; publish the requirement-to-evidence register and any non-blocking known issues.
Verify the exact shipping binaries, commit/tag/release artifacts and declare the game complete only after the release gate is satisfied.

acceptance: M00–M31 are complete with reviewed evidence, every required acceptance scenario passes, and no P0/P1 defect remains open.
The actual shipped Linux/Windows packages launch, play, save, reload and recover correctly using only documented player dependencies.
The shipped build meets the accepted feature scope, visual/interaction targets and measured performance/balance gates; optional future ideas stay separate from the completed 1.0 scope.

release_scenarios: Survival: configurable new game → move in → queue and meet needs → actual paid work → device purchase → real delivery → better housing → vehicle/business asset → ownership opportunity or refusal.
Manager: actual budget/staffing → planned funded construction → compensation or contested eviction → working profitable facility → emergency response/repair → succession or move-out game over.
Cheat: roleplay and inspect/possess residents → bounded edits to all supported rules/entities → coherent world, accounting and saves.
Conflict: queue cut/theft → witnesses/report → physical combat/surrender → evidence-based enforcement → cell/escape/rescue → actual release/recovered property.
Disaster: disease/fire/structural damage → warning/evacuation → staffed paid response → treatment/death/body handling → estate/claims → funded physical recovery.
Continuity: old native/browser import → preserve identities/titles/prepaid work/families → play each relevant system → save in another named slot → reload/recover after a corrupt primary.

change_log.change: Created the fixed sequential plan at the user’s request. Gameplay-first phase order follows the accepted priorities. Existing implementation is the baseline, not discarded work. No new gameplay milestone is marked complete by this planning-only change.

Completed the one-time M00 inventory: 38 requirements, 14 parity decisions, frozen source manifests, 38 acceptance scenarios, ranked gaps and isolated hardware/headless/rendered baseline. Advanced to M01.1 without adding scope or restarting delivered systems.

Completed M01.1: persistent directional social opinions and private actual-event memories, localized nearby history, relevant aid/estate integration and verified regressions. Closed D-M00-01. M01 remains active; next task is M01.2 information transfer.

open_defects.description: Imported family, pregnancy and births remain archive-only and do not continue natively.
Interior edits cannot yet create arbitrary partial slab openings with shared support/navigation/rendering.
Vehicles lack the accepted fuller rolling/support/overturning and furniture contact model.
Video work scores clip ordering but has no actual trim/timeline workflow.
Custody uses an intake footprint instead of individually lockable occupied cells and real restraint equipment.
Large default floor areas remain mostly vacant and do not reach the supplied reference interior density.
Cheat lacks the complete bounded entity/world-rule editor.
Browser history charts/CSV export have no complete native UI equivalent.

resolved_defects.description: Combat/theft have no persistent directional encounter memory; a victim can retain the same social regard for the offender.
resolved_defects.resolution: M01.1; assault regression now changes victim trust from 0 to -0.85, with private directional history and save compatibility verified.
